images.name: cover
images.title: What an *AI Employee* can't do (and shouldn't)
images.sub: The limits that come with the technology, and the ones a business should set on purpose.

images.name: cant-vs-shouldnt
images.title: What it *can't* do, and what it *shouldn't*
head: Can't do at all
Shouldn't do, even though it could
rows: Make promises outside the written policy
See a leak or check a parcel
Decide an unclear emergency from a photo
Hold a licence or sign for the business
Give legal, medical, tax or investment advice
Refund past a set limit or change anyone's pay
Hire, fire, discipline, or handle someone upset
Do anything that can't be undone
images.source: Every item in the right column needs a written rule

images.name: by-industry
images.title: Where the line sits in *five kinds of business*
rows: Books, reschedules and sends reminders from the schedule
Says a clinician will call back and flags it to the front desk
Collects the details and books the consultation after a conflict check
Logs it, asks for photos and books the trade
Online store: refund over the limit
Prepares it with the order history and waits for approval
Tells them the account lead will call today

images.name: three-questions
images.title: Three questions that *sort any duty*
steps: Can a mistake be undone easily?
Rebooking an appointment can. A final notice to a client can't.
Does it need a licence, signature or name?
If yes, the AI Employee prepares and the professional decides.
Is money, health or a job on the line?
Or is the person on the other end upset? Then a person handles it.
It goes to the AI Employee alone, or with a report back.
It stays with a person, and the AI Employee does the preparation.

images.name: quote
images.text: Most problems start the same way. Someone asked what the AI could do, and *never wrote down what it shouldn't.*
